review_notes:
I reviewed the whole supplied file, including the LE/LT inductives, the simp lemmas, and the Preorder, PartialOrder, SemilatticeSup/Inf, DistribLattice, BoundedOrder and BooleanAlgebra instances. I did not read other files or search the source roots.

The structure is repetitive but the repetition is not nontrivial shared reasoning. The `lift_le_*` and `lift_lt_*` simp lemmas use the same `rintro ⟨_⟩; assumption` pattern, but each is a one-line routine inversion. The SemilatticeSup and SemilatticeInf instances are order-dual case analyses. They use different API (`sdiff_le`, `disjoint_sdiff_self_right`, `le_sdiff`, `sup_le`, `le_inf`), and every case is one or two terms. The `le_sup_inf` cases each use a different sdiff identity (`sup_sdiff`, `sdiff_inf`, `sdiff_sdiff_right'`). The `inf_compl_le_bot`, `top_le_sup_compl` and `sdiff_eq` goals are all closed by `simp`, so no proof is duplicated.

A shared lemma would only move case branches around or wrap existing API, which the rubric says is insufficient. I found no justified finding.
